memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The Lord alone led him; no foreign god was with him. He made him ride on the heights of the land and fed him with the fruit of the fields. He nourished him with honey from the rock, and with oil from the flinty crag, with curds and milk from herd and flock and with fattened lambs and goats, with choice rams of Bashan and the finest kernels of wheat. You drank the foaming blood of the grape." — Deut 32:12-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses emphasises that God "alone led" His people — no foreign god helped, no other power shared the credit. And then he describes God's lavish provision in rich, almost overflowing language: honey from the rock, oil from the flinty crag, the finest of everything. God did not merely keep His people alive; He blessed them abundantly, drawing sweetness even from hard places — "honey from the rock."

That phrase is worth savouring. God brought sweetness out of the flinty crag, nourishment from barren stone. This is what our God delights to do — to provide in ways that seem impossible, to bring blessing out of the hardest and most unlikely places. Where we see only bare rock, God can bring honey.

We should be careful not to twist this into a promise that God will always make us materially rich. This was God's particular, abundant care for Israel, and it points to His generous character rather than guaranteeing us luxury. But the truth stands: our God is a generous provider, and He can bring good even out of hard circumstances.

And notice — "the Lord alone led him." God wants us to look to Him alone, not to divide our trust between Him and other "gods" of money, status, or self. He alone is our leader and provider. Ultimately, every good gift points to the greatest gift, His Son, through whom God graciously gives us all things (Rom 8:32). Trust the God who leads you alone and provides even honey from the rock.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I look to God alone, or divide my trust among other "gods"?
2. Where has God brought unexpected "honey from the rock" in my life?
3. How can I thank God for His generous provision today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You alone have led me and provided for me, bringing sweetness even from hard places. Help me trust You alone and see Your generous hand. Thank You for every good gift, above all Your Son. Amen.
